newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma gives Thai PM red carpet welcome.
newsitem.headline: Burma gives Thai PM red carpet welcome.

text.p: Burma's military leaders gave Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh a warm welcome when he arrived in Rangoon on Friday for a short visit aimed at strengthening bilateral ties.

The head of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) and Prime Minister General Than Shwe, his deputy General Maung Aye and the powerful SLORC Secretary One, Lieutenant-General Khin Nyunt, were at the airport to meet him.
Chavalit, who returns to Bangkok on Saturday, was given a 19-gun salute when he inspected a guard of honour and thousands of school children waved Thai and Burmese flags.
The premier was scheduled to meet key Burmese leaders later on Friday for talks.
He was expected to discuss problems caused by the more than 700,000 illegal Burmese workers in Thailand and to review nagging border disputes.
Chavalit would also discuss Burma's imminent entry into the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), Thai sources said.
Burma, along with Laos and Cambodia, is expected to join ASEAN later this year. The group comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Its entry into ASEAN is opposed by the United States.
Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn was expected to sign a "Cross Border Agreement" with his Burmese counterpart Ohn Gyaw.
One Rangoon political analyst played down the importance of the visit
"This is a symbolic visit. I dont think there will be major agenda items discussed. The leaders of the two countries will focus on bilateral issues," the analyst said.

Although Thailand is the third largest investor in Burma, where official records show Thai investment at the end of April at $1.026 billion, there would be no business deals signed during Chavalit's visit, analysts said.
They said this had no connection with Washington's decision to impose economic sanctions on Burma last month over the military regime's human rights record.
